source_semantics.visibility: The canonical SiteOperationsMaintenance header renders an Operations hub anchor alongside the separate Refresh and Operation history controls.
source_semantics.navigation: The canonical Operations hub control is a read-only anchor from both maintenance route aliases to /operations.
source_semantics.scope_boundary: Refresh, Operation history, preview refresh, cleanup confirmation and cleanup execution are distinct canonical operations and are not claimed by this closure.
source_semantics.mutation: Opening the Operations hub performs navigation only and does not mutate operation-history persistence or invoke WordPress/provider behavior.

laravel_adaptation.source_routes: The already-terminal explicit tenant-scoped /tenants/{tenant}/operations/maintenance and /tenants/{tenant}/site-operations/maintenance routes remain the real source pages.
laravel_adaptation.target: Both source pages render the canonical marker on an Operations hub link targeting the existing named canonical.workspace.operations route for the authoritative active tenant. No new route or API is introduced.
laravel_adaptation.tenant_derivation: OperationsMaintenanceReadController and SiteOperationsMaintenanceReadController verify the route tenant against TenantContext and pass the active tenant slug to the view; the link does not accept a caller-supplied destination or resource identifier.
laravel_adaptation.permission_alignment: The maintenance pages retain their existing execution.view read boundary. The Operations hub control is additionally suppressed unless the active membership has operations.manage because the existing target independently requires operations.manage and execution.view.
laravel_adaptation.read_only: The control performs no persistence, queue, approval, execution, provider or WordPress mutation.

tenant_and_security.cross_tenant: TenantContext remains authoritative for both source aliases and target; a member of Alpha cannot open Beta maintenance or Operations hub paths.
tenant_and_security.identifier_minimization: The href contains only the trusted tenant slug and no site, history, execution, approval or arbitrary return URL identifier.
tenant_and_security.dead_control_prevention: A membership that may read maintenance with execution.view but lacks operations.manage receives no Operations hub control; direct target access remains forbidden.
tenant_and_security.external_runtime: This operation is navigation-only and requires no live WordPress, AI provider, email, payment, DNS or production mutation evidence.

proofs: exact canonical operation identity, source screen aliases, visible-control fingerprint, read-only flag and tenant ownership
both real maintenance aliases render the same tenant-bound Operations hub control for a membership satisfying target permissions
the control targets only the existing named canonical.workspace.operations route for the active tenant
the existing target route independently retains auth, tenant.context, operations.manage and execution.view guards
maintenance remains readable but the control is hidden when operations.manage is absent, while direct target access returns 403
Alpha-to-Beta source and target paths fail closed with 404
reading the source aliases and target does not change operation-history persistence
acceptance.repository_ci: Focused validation plus normal PR-head security/parity/acceptance gates and canonical generator enrollment are required before integration; exact run identifiers are recorded on the PR and Issue #257 only after they complete.
